legal.notice: This is a demonstration project built for an academic course (Bachelor 2). It is not legal advice: the texts below describe how this application actually works.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains which personal data the application stores, why, who can see it and how you stay in control.

summary.a: We store only what the service needs to run.
summary.b: We never sell your data and never use it for advertising.
summary.c: We do not use tracking cookies.
summary.d: You can edit your details and ask for your account to be deactivated.

data.title: 1. Data we collect
data.body: When you create an account we store your email address, first name, last name, phone number and, optionally, a postal address. When you order, book a table or join the queue, we also store what you ordered, the date and time, the table and the size of your party.

purpose.title: 2. Why we collect it
purpose.body: Only to run the service: sign you in, take and follow an order, confirm a reservation, hold your place in the queue and issue an invoice. We never sell data and we do not use it for advertising or profiling.

retention.title: 3. How long we keep it
retention.body: Your account and its orders stay in the database for the duration of the demonstration. The demonstration data can be reset at any time with the backend’s seed command.

access.title: 4. Who can see it
access.body: You see your own data. Staff see the customers, orders, reservations and queue of the restaurant. The administrator sees every account, as the person in charge of the system.

cookies.title: 5. Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: We do not set tracking cookies. Your browser stores only what the application needs: a refresh token that keeps you signed in, your cart, the table you scanned, and your theme and language choices. Clearing your browser data removes all of it.

security.title: 6. How we protect it
security.body: Passwords are never stored in clear text: the server keeps only a hash. Your session uses a short-lived access token held in memory and a refresh token that is replaced each time it is used. Signing out invalidates the refresh token, and the server checks your role again on every request.

rights.title: 7. Your rights
rights.body: You can change your name and contact details from the profile page, change your password from the password page, and ask the administrator to deactivate your account. Deactivating an account signs you out everywhere.

changes.title: 8. Changes to this policy
changes.body: If the application starts to store new kinds of data, this page is updated first. The date at the top shows the latest revision.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: These terms describe what you can expect from the application and what we ask of you when you use it.

summary.a: The application is a demonstration: no real money is charged.
summary.b: Keep your password private and do not share your account.
summary.c: Prices are set by the restaurant; the cart only shows an estimate.
summary.d: Use the service for its purpose and respect other users.

service.title: 1. The service
service.body: Maisha is a table, queue and online ordering application. It lets customers browse the menu, book a table, join the queue, place an order, pay for it and read their invoices.

account.title: 2. Your account
account.body: Keep your password private and do not share your account. Deactivating an account is the only way to close it, and the data is kept for the duration of the demonstration.

orders.title: 3. Orders and payments
orders.body: Prices are set and computed by the restaurant’s server; the cart shows an estimate. Card and mobile money payments are simulated in this demonstration and no real money is charged. Cash payments are confirmed by a member of staff.

reservations.title: 4. Reservations and the queue
reservations.body: A reservation depends on the free time slots shown when you book, and you can cancel it from your reservations page. You can leave the queue at any time. Staff may adjust reservations and queue entries when the restaurant is busy.

conduct.title: 5. Acceptable use
conduct.body: Use the service for its purpose. Do not try to reach other people’s data, overload the service or bypass its security.

ip.title: 6. Intellectual property
ip.body: The code was written for this project. The dish names and descriptions come from the demonstration data.

liability.title: 7. Responsibility
liability.body: This is an academic demonstration. The service is provided as is, without any guarantee of uninterrupted availability.

law.title: 8. Applicable law
law.body: For information only, the project is built in Burundi. This text has no legal value; it describes how the demonstration works.
